To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the risk for testicular endocrine failure after treatment of haematologic malignancy in children and teenagers is not negligible.
the testicular endocrine functions of patients treated for haematological malignancies are not impaired by the standard chemotherapy protocols.

the testicular endocrine status in children and adolescents with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) treated according to the standard protocols is normal, and that the treatment of ALL does not affect the testicular endocrinological function.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the evaluation of testicular endocrine status in children and teenagers treated with chemotherapy and radiotherapy for haematological malignancies, with a special focus on the role of GnRH analogs in the prevention of chemotherapy-induced gonadotoxicity.

the safety of standardised treatments (chemotherapy and/or radiotherapy) for haematologic diseases in children and teenagers as regards to testis endocrine function, in particular spermatogenesis and fertility.
the safety of chemotherapy for haematologic diseases as regards to the testicular endocrine functions of children and adolescents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the testicular endocrine functions are not compromised in patients treated for haematologic diseases, including ALL, AML and NHL, with standardised chemotherapy protocols.
there is insufficient evidence to recommend the use of GnRH agonists or testosterone in the prevention of testicular damage in boys treated with standardised chemotherapy regimens.
there is no significant risk to testicular endocrinological function in boys treated for haematological malignancies with standardised chemotherapy regimens.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results of the present research indicate that the use of the standard treatments for haematological malignancies is connected with the risk of testicular endocrine dysfunction.
the safety of chemotherapy for testicular endocrine purpose in kids and teenagers is unknown.
the safety of chemotherapy and radiotherapy for haematologic neoplasms as regards to endocrine function is well known, and the majority of the patients will recover normal function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we should be more careful about using these drugs, especially in children.
we should not be so quick to dismiss the possibility of a genetic contribution to the risk of developing testicular cancer, even in men with a history of cryptorchidism.
there is no significant impact on testicular endocrine functions in children and teenagers treated for haematologic neoplasms.
